prompt:
Return exactly one bare JSON object with keys name, phone, email, company, country. Each value must be a string or JSON null. No Markdown or prose.

1. Isolate the single contact block in the user's note. Labels may vary, lines may be shuffled, and separators may be colons, equals signs or tabs. Use only those label/value lines. Never use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes to fill or change another field. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these whole-value placeholders, ignoring case, as null: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.
2. Assign values containing @ to email regardless of label. Assign phone-like values to phone regardless of label: after removing a leading tel: and any trailing extension (ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits), the value must have at least seven digits and contain only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. Take country only from the country line, subject to step 5. Swap the name-line and company-line values if the former ends in a legal suffix and the latter does not. The suffix list, matched case-insensitively, is: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.
3. Normalize the text fields. Name: move the part before the first comma after the part following it; drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof (any case, optional dot). For each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase its first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration. Company: remove the trailing legal suffix and any optional comma immediately before it, trim, and uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets wherever one wraps the other, then lowercase the whole address.
4. Normalize a present country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, case-insensitively: UK or Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA or U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
5. Normalize a present phone to E.164 (+ and digits only). Use the number without tel: or the extension. Ignore a leading opening parenthesis when checking whether it starts with + or 00. If international, remove (0), strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and replace initial 00 with +. Keep the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If country is missing, infer it only if this code belongs to one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. This is the only exception to the missing-value rule. If national, strip separators, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code. If country is missing, set a national phone to null.
